articles.title: A city of light for Northwind Architects
articles.intro: A new identity and portfolio site for an architecture practice whose buildings change colour with the hour.
articles.full:
The brief

Northwind had outgrown a template website that showed its buildings as small, grey thumbnails. They wanted a home that felt like walking through their work.

What we did

We built a modular identity around the warm glass of their towers, and a website where every project opens full-screen, with drawings, materials and a timeline of the build.

Fast, thoughtful and calm under pressure. We would hire them again tomorrow.

Results

  • 3× longer visits
  • 41% more enquiries
  • 8 weeks from kickoff to launch
Client
Northwind Architects
Services
Brand identity, Web design
articles.image_alt: Orange glass towers seen from below
articles.author: Mara Ellis

articles.title: Seeing the grid with Halden Energy
articles.intro: A live dashboard that turns two hundred wind turbines into one clear picture for the people who run them.
articles.full:
The brief

Halden's operators watched six different tools to keep an offshore wind farm running. Alarms were missed, and new staff took months to learn the systems.

What we did

We spent two weeks in the control room, then designed and built one dashboard: a map of the farm, the turbines that need attention first, and the weather that will matter next.

They listened first and designed second. It shows in every screen.

Results

  • 62% faster response to alarms
  • 1 screen instead of six
  • 99.98% uptime since launch
Client
Halden Energy
Services
Product design, Engineering
articles.image_alt: Offshore wind turbines at sea
articles.author: Ines Kovač

articles.title: The Aperture museum after dark
articles.intro: An exhibition website for a museum of light, built to feel as playful as the rooms it describes.
articles.full:
The brief

The museum's night programme sold out in person but barely existed online. They needed a site that could sell tickets and carry the atmosphere of the galleries.

What we did

Every exhibition gets a page of moving light made with plain CSS and a few lines of script, so it loads fast on a phone in a queue outside. Tickets take three taps.

They listened first and designed second. It shows in every screen.

Results

  • 2.1 s largest contentful paint on 4G
  • +54% online ticket sales
  • 0 third-party scripts
Client
Aperture Museum of Light
Services
Web design, Motion
articles.image_alt: Red and blue streaks of light over water at night
articles.author: Mara Ellis

articles.title: Vela Towers, from launch to living room
articles.intro: A launch campaign for two residential towers, from the hoarding on the street to the welcome pack on the kitchen table.
articles.full:
The brief

Vela had a remarkable building and a crowded market. The first homes had to sell before the second tower topped out.

What we did

We named the towers, designed the identity around their twist, and ran one campaign across print, street and a small, quick website with floor plans that work on any screen.

The new work feels like us, only clearer. Our customers noticed within a week.

Results

  • 78% of homes reserved before completion
  • 12 weeks of campaign
  • 5 design awards
Client
Vela Residences
Services
Brand identity, Campaign
articles.image_alt: A twisting tower lit at night
articles.author: Mara Ellis

articles.title: Outdoor gear for Aurora Outfitters
articles.intro: A new shop for an outdoor brand whose customers buy on the move, often on a weak signal at the edge of the map.
articles.full:
The brief

Aurora's old shop was slow, and half of their customers left before the product page had loaded. Returns were high because sizes were hard to judge.

What we did

We rebuilt the shop around speed and clarity: small pages, images sized for each screen, a size guide drawn from real returns, and a checkout that survives a dropped connection.

They listened first and designed second. It shows in every screen.

Results

  • −38% returns
  • +27% mobile conversion
  • 1.4 s average page load
Client
Aurora Outfitters
Services
E-commerce, Web design
articles.image_alt: Green and red polar lights over a forest
articles.author: Ines Kovač

articles.title: An open data platform for the city
articles.intro: A developer platform that publishes a city's open data with documentation people actually enjoy reading.
articles.full:
The brief

The city released hundreds of data sets a year, but few developers used them: formats changed without notice and the documentation was a set of PDFs.

What we did

We designed a versioned API, a catalogue with search and previews, and documentation written alongside the code, so every example is tested before it is published.

They turned a complicated problem into something our whole team understands.

Results

  • 340 data sets published
  • 5× more API keys issued
  • 100% of examples tested
Client
Open City Data
Services
Engineering, Product design
articles.image_alt: Two screens with code on a dark desk
articles.author: Theo Brandt

articles.title: A furniture brand with holes in all the right places
articles.intro: An identity for a young furniture maker, drawn from the perforated steel at the heart of its first collection.
articles.full:
The brief

Perfora had one beautiful collection, a tiny budget and no name customers could remember.

What we did

We named the company after its material and built the whole identity from a grid of round holes: the logo, a typeface of dots, flat-pack boxes and a one-page shop.

Fast, thoughtful and calm under pressure. We would hire them again tomorrow.

Results

  • 1 grid behind everything
  • 3 retailers signed in the first month
  • 0 plastic in the packaging
Client
Perfora
Services
Brand identity, Packaging
articles.image_alt: A white perforated building against a teal sky
articles.author: Mara Ellis

articles.title: Spiral Records, around and around
articles.intro: A refreshed identity and a listening-first website for an independent record label celebrating twenty years.
articles.full:
The brief

After twenty years and four hundred releases, Spiral's catalogue was scattered across platforms and its own site had not changed in a decade.

What we did

We gave the logo a quarter turn and built a site where the whole catalogue plays in the browser, release by release, with liner notes written by the artists.

They listened first and designed second. It shows in every screen.

Results

  • 400 releases online
  • +65% direct sales
  • 20 years celebrated
Client
Spiral Records
Services
Brand identity, Web design, Motion
articles.image_alt: A white and yellow spiral staircase from above
articles.author: Mara Ellis

articles.title: Quiet infrastructure for Cirrus Hosting
articles.intro: A control panel for a hosting company that wanted its customers to forget their servers were there.
articles.full:
The brief

Cirrus had fast, reliable servers and a control panel that generated more support tickets than any outage.

What we did

We mapped the twenty tasks customers do most, designed one clear path for each, and rebuilt the panel as a set of small, accessible components the Cirrus team now owns.

They listened first and designed second. It shows in every screen.

Results

  • −45% support tickets
  • 20 tasks redesigned
  • AA WCAG level met
Client
Cirrus Hosting
Services
Product design, Engineering
articles.image_alt: Rows of servers lit blue in a data centre
articles.author: Sam Okoye
